evidence: Swap test fails: an equipment-hire shop, a bike-share or a library-of-things in any town could use the frame unchanged; only the copy (deposits, 'Open' sessions, desk phone number) is bound to Fernhill.
Identity is the name 'Fernhill Tool Library' set in bold body type beside a stock wrench outline (masthead, all routes); no mark, no ground or material from the library's world.
Every tool card on / uses the same wrench icon in a pale-green square instead of an image of the tool (items-ladder-3m/default/1280-light.png, 10 of 10 cards).
Category-guess: pale near-white ground, one forest-green accent, white bordered cards, a humanist sans and a line icon is the predicted default for a community/eco service.
Similar-prompt: 'reservation for a community seed library / toy library' would land on the same green-on-pale, card grid, wrench-or-leaf thumbnail frame.

Product-bound elements that do exist: the pick-up calendar marking 'Open' session days (tool page), availability badges 'Available from Sat 10 Oct', volunteer-voice copy ('returned when it comes back clean and working').

sections that are only a heading and a list or text: 'Opening times', 'Details', 'What happens next'

Tool page: the calendar's large empty white cells at 1280 are the biggest element yet read as a form grid; the sticky action bar's button sits flush to the window edge, out of the content column.

Clean and orderly throughout; dark theme is composed and consistent, but bare.
